clue.text: Part diners are happy to be repeating

definitions.note: a part is a role in a play; Yum-Yum is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado

indicators.note: repeating says the word for a satisfied diner's noise is written down twice in a row

parts.note: yum is what diners say when the food pleases them

explanation.surface: Diners at a restaurant are so pleased they keep saying it over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like 'some of the diners', but it is the definition: a stage role in The Mikado, the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical role: Yum-Yum is the young heroine in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera The Mikado.

clue.text: Got you starting over, taking time for dessert

indicators.note: taking says the jumbled letters take in the time word inside them
starting picks the opening letter of the word you
over here means done again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone caught out has to start again, and takes their time choosing a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges the jumble into YOGT before 'taking' wraps it round the time word; YOGHOURT is an older spelling of yogurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt, here in an older spelling, is eaten as a sweet course after a meal.

clue.text: Pie filling scruffy team after getting the chop?

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled team behind the chopping word

parts.note: to mince is to chop food finely

indicators.note: scruffy says the letters of team are untidily jumbled

explanation.surface: A shabby sports team is being sacked, as if fit only to be pie filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the chop' sounds like being sacked, but it gives MINCE; 'scruffy' turns TEAM into MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat, a spiced dried-fruit mixture, fills the small pies eaten in Britain at Christmas.

clue.text: No! (though "yes" when husband's in the middle)

parts.words: though "yes" when husband's in the middle
parts.note: putting H, the abbreviation for husband, in the middle turns the grunt of refusal into uh-huh, the grunt of agreement

explanation.surface: A refusal that would become an acceptance if a husband stepped into the middle of it.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the usual abbreviation for husband; slot it between the two halves and the refusing grunt becomes UH-HUH, which means yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is an informal spoken grunt used to refuse or disagree.

clue.text: A fool picking the wrong date becomes distressed

parts.note: git is British slang for a stupid or contemptible person

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of date are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A fool who has booked the wrong day for something gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for an idiot; 'wrong' rearranges DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone anxious and upset; they are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Animal's mistake lets in little bird

indicators.note: lets in says one piece is admitted inside the other

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

indicators.note: little here means the word bird shrunk to its inner letters, ends dropped

explanation.surface: An animal's blunder allows a small bird inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little bird' reads as a small bird, but 'little' trims bird to its middle, IR, which goes into GAFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall long-necked African mammal is a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Cut red linen to different shape

indicators.note: putting into a different shape means the letters of red linen and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut some red linen into a different shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a sewing instruction, but it is the definition: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of beef or pork, taken from beside the backbone.

clue.text: There's a light in Brentor church

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words Brentor church, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A lamp is lit inside the church at Brentor, a Dartmoor village.
explanation.walkthrough: Brentor is a village on Dartmoor in Devon, famous for its hilltop church.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, what Americans call a flashlight.

clue.text: Mess up in medics' sinks

indicators.note: in says the upturned mess goes inside the doctors

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors, medics

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: poo is a childish word for excrement, a mess

explanation.surface: Somebody has made a mess in the doctors' washbasins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' looks like basins, but it is a verb: the definition is to sag or droop.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink and to droop both mean to sag or drop lower; here both are verbs.

clue.text: Meddles with reversible implements

indicators.note: reversible says the word for these implements is turned round

parts.note: spoons are eating implements

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers with tools that can be turned either way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To pry into other people's affairs is to meddle; both are verbs in the same form.

clue.text: Criminal trader gives cue to Jock to get away

parts.note: the starter's gun gives the cue for a race to begin
a jock is an athlete, here a runner, who sets off at the gun

explanation.surface: A villainous dealer prompts a Scotsman to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' looks like the slang for a Scot, but here it is the American slang for an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunrunner is someone who smuggles and sells weapons illegally.

clue.text: Informant spoken to finally by man from drug squad

indicators.note: spoken says the word for informant is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a nark is British slang for a police informer

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word to

explanation.surface: A police informer talks to an officer from the narcotics unit.
explanation.walkthrough: NARK, British slang for an informer, sounds like NARC; add O, the last letter of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is American slang for a narcotics officer, an agent policing illegal substances.

clue.text: Moreover, it contains biscuit

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held inside the word Moreover

explanation.surface: An aside that something, moreover, has a cookie in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oreo is a brand of chocolate sandwich cookie with a cream filling.

clue.text: A new opening for sweets bound for cafe

indicators.note: a new opening means the first letter of the sweets is swapped for another

parts.note: toffees are chewy sweets
to hop is to bound or leap

explanation.surface: Fresh sweets on sale at a new shop, destined for a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is left for the solver to find: the crossings and the definition fix it as C.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee shop is a small casual cafe serving drinks and snacks.

clue.text: Complains of complaints

definitions.meaning: a verb: to grumble or moan
stomach pains are complaints in the medical sense

explanation.walkthrough: The same letters read as one word are a verb, moaning; read as two they are tummy upsets, medical complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling is bellyaching, and pains in the stomach are literally belly aches.

clue.text: Visionary official involved in about-turn on cigarettes

indicators.note: an about-turn means the whole assembly is turned to face the other way
involved in says the official goes inside the visionary

parts.note: a seer is a prophet, a visionary
ref is short for referee, a sports official

explanation.surface: A prophet and a referee are caught up in a U-turn over smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: REF goes into SEER to give SREFEER; 'about-turn' then reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefers are cannabis cigarettes, joints in slang.

clue.text: Is this where Juncker is hiding cake?

parts.note: Jean-Claude Juncker was president of the EC, the European Commission
a lair is a hiding place, a den

explanation.surface: A question about where a European Union boss is lying low with a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EC LAIR, the answer is the European Commission's den, where its president Juncker hides out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long pastry of choux filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Hi sir!

parts.note: read as wordplay, a stew of the word Irish, that is a jumble of its letters, produces this greeting

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the instruction, with 'stew' as the anagram signal, that would turn IRISH into the clue's HI SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a dish of mutton, potatoes and onions, and as wordplay it means the letters Irish jumbled.

clue.text: Close to alcohol, but not enough

definitions.text: Close to alcohol, but not enough

parts.note: near means close to
beer is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Something almost a drink, but falling short of the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a drink that is nearly beer but lacks the strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Near beer is malt drink with very little or no alcohol, sold as a substitute.

clue.text: Hot stuff! Christmas cake reduced by £1

indicators.note: reduced by says the cake loses the money symbol's letter

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas
one pound is written with L, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Christmas cake marked down by a pound is a bargain, a hot item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff!' sounds like an exclamation about spice, but 'Hot' means stolen; 'stuff' is a link meaning goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, of goods taken illegally and risky to handle.

clue.text: Ultimate enlightenment for rock band

definitions.meaning: in Buddhism the final state of freedom from suffering and rebirth
the Seattle grunge group fronted by Kurt Cobain

explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist goal of release, and also the name of the 1990s grunge rock group.

clue.text: Fancy licentious lot being carried away by cookery

indicators.note: fancy says the letters are rearranged in an elaborate new way
being carried away says the letters of lot leave the pool

explanation.surface: Dissolute people swept up in a passion for elaborate cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L, O and T out of LICENTIOUS ('being carried away') and rearrange the rest ('Fancy').
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cooking, as in French or Italian cuisine.

clue.text: Winners get Irish dish — and seconds

parts.note: champ is an Irish dish of mashed potato with spring onions

explanation.surface: The victors get a plate of Irish food and go back for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like a second helping, but it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Champs is a short informal word for champions, those who win.

clue.text: Two soft drinks taken outside by Jonathan and Granny Smith

indicators.note: taken outside says the drinks are placed around the soft letters

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft, so two of them give PP

explanation.surface: Two fizzy drinks are carried outside by two people called Jonathan and Granny Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drinks' reads as one phrase, a fizzy drink, but 'soft' is the musical piano sign, doubled by 'Two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan and Granny Smith are both varieties of eating fruit from the orchard tree.

clue.text: Did it contribute to revitalised bap trade?

definitions.text: Did it contribute to revitalised bap trade?

indicators.note: revitalised says the letters are given new life in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a flatbread revived the market for bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a soft British bread roll; IT plus BAP TRADE, 'revitalised', gives the answer, itself a bread that might boost the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread, a plausible rival or boost to the trade in rolls.

clue.text: Starts the orchestral number, addressing lightness of sound quality

indicators.note: starts says to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An orchestra begins a piece with a light, delicate tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal is an adjective about tone, the character of a musical sound.

clue.text: Drink to Cockney individual; not a vocal actor

indicators.note: not says the spoken actor is removed from the individual

parts.note: a character is an individual, a person

indicators.note: vocal says the word actor is said out loud, its sound matching the end of the individual

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: Toasting a Cockney character who is not a voice actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners; their slang 'char' means tea. ACTER, which sounds like 'actor', comes off the end of CHARACTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is British slang for tea, a word associated with London's Cockney speech.

clue.text: Swimmers want to have fresh start instead

indicators.note: instead says one letter of the wanting word is replaced by another

parts.note: to wish is to want

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the word fresh

explanation.surface: Swimmers wishing for a new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'fresh' takes the place of W at the front of WISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish are creatures that swim; the plural is the same as the singular.

clue.text: It's not half madness to take a little Cheddar at this time

indicators.note: not half means only the front half of the word for madness is kept

parts.note: lunacy is madness
a little of the word Cheddar is its first two letters, Ch

explanation.surface: It is half crazy to eat a bit of cheese at this hour.
explanation.walkthrough: LUNACY halved gives LUN, then add CH from the start of 'Cheddar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch names the midday mealtime, so a time of day.

clue.text: New incumbent Spike in "A Call of Nature"

indicators.note: in says the spike goes inside the call of nature

parts.note: a pee is an act of urinating, answering a call of nature
a point is a sharp tip, a spike

explanation.surface: A newly appointed man called Spike stars in a play titled A Call of Nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a person's name and the quotation like a title, but both are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is a person newly given a post, its new holder.

clue.text: Girl sent to Texas — trumped-up charge

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

indicators.note: trumped-up means made up, so the letters of Texas are invented afresh

explanation.surface: A woman is sent to Texas on a fabricated accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumped-up charge' reads as one false accusation, but 'charge' is the definition, a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales tax is a levy added to the price of goods, a charge on purchases.

clue.text: Undesirables at baby's party

definitions.meaning: British slang for a useless or contemptible group of people
a baby ... is a gift party for a mother-to-be

explanation.definitionFit: Shower is British slang for a bad lot of people, and also a party bringing gifts for an expected baby.
